views.name: classroom_core
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  classroom.building AS building,
  classroom.room_number AS room_number,
  classroom.capacity AS capacity
FROM classroom
views.description: Canonical classroom rows with key columns and raw attributes; cleans/normalizes values for reuse (no question-specific filters).

views.name: classroom_capacity_cohort
views.body_sql:
SELECT building, room_number, capacity
FROM classroom_core
views.description: Subset cohort of classrooms including capacity as a measure so callers can apply capacity thresholds and other filters.

views.name: section_room_assignment
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  s.course_id,
  s.sec_id,
  s.semester,
  s.year,
  s.building,
  s.room_number,
  s.time_slot_id,
  c.capacity
FROM section AS s
LEFT JOIN classroom AS c
  ON s.building = c.building
  AND s.room_number = c.room_number
views.description: Denormalized mapping of sections to the classroom they use (one row per section) including the classroom capacity — useful for queries that compare enrolled size or section attributes to room capacity.

views.name: classroom_rows
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  classroom.building AS building,
  classroom.room_number AS room_number,
  classroom.capacity AS capacity
FROM classroom
views.description: Canonical row-level view of classroom records (one row per classroom) exposing building and room and capacity for filtering, grouping, and counting.
validated_on: Determine the number of classrooms categorized as 'Large', 'Medium', or 'Small' based on their capacities in the 'Lamberton' building, with only those classrooms having a capacity greater than 20 included in the count.

views.name: classroom_counts_by_building
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  classroom.building AS building,
  COUNT(*) AS classroom_count
FROM classroom
GROUP BY classroom.building
views.description: Pre-aggregated counts of classrooms per building. One row per building with the raw count of classroom rows; useful for ranking or filtering buildings by number of rooms.

views.name: classroom_capacity_by_building
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  building,
  COUNT(room_number) AS classroom_count,
  SUM(capacity) AS total_capacity
FROM classroom
GROUP BY building
views.description: Aggregate measures per building: total number of classrooms and total seating capacity. One row per building to support questions comparing room counts and capacity.

views.name: department_basic
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  d.dept_name,
  d.building,
  d.budget
FROM department d
views.description: One row per department with its canonical dept_name, building, and raw budget for filtering or aggregation.
validated_on: What are the names and buildings of the first three departments when ordered alphabetically by department name?
Hey! Can you tell me how many different departments have courses with more than 3 credits?
What is the total number of distinct courses offered by the Physics department?
Could you provide the average budget for each department?

views.name: department_budget_stats
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  d.dept_name AS dept_name,
  (SELECT AVG(budget) FROM department) AS avg_budget
FROM department d
GROUP BY d.dept_name
views.description: Aggregate budget statistics across all departments (used to compare individual department budgets to overall averages). Produces one row for the global aggregation and can be joined to department_basic for comparisons.

views.name: departments_with_location_and_budget
views.body_sql:
SELECT department.dept_name AS dept_name,
       department.building AS building,
       department.budget AS budget
FROM department
views.description: Denormalized department rows exposing dept_name, building, and budget for straightforward selection and output. Same grain as department row.

views.name: department_core
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  dept_name,
  building,
  budget
FROM department
views.description: One row per department with its core attributes (dept name, building, budget). Useful as the department cohort for filters, joins, and budget comparisons.
validated_on: What are the names and buildings of the first three departments when ordered alphabetically by department name?
Could you provide the average budget for each department?

views.name: top_instructor_per_department
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  dept_name,
  ID AS "ID AS instructor_id",
  name AS "name AS instructor_name",
  salary AS "salary AS instructor_salary",
  ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY dept_name ORDER BY salary DESC) AS "ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY dept_name ORDER BY salary DESC) AS rn"
FROM instructor
output_columns: ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY dept_name ORDER BY salary DESC) AS rn
views.description: For each department (dept_name), rank instructors by salary descending and expose the top-ranked instructor(s). Returns one row per instructor; use row_number = 1 to select a single highest-paid instructor per department. This view does NOT apply department-name or budget filters so it can be reused for different department cohorts.

views.name: classroom_rows_11
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  building,
  room_number,
  capacity
FROM classroom
views.description: Canonical classroom rows exposing building, room identifier and numeric capacity.

views.name: building_classroom_capacity_agg
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  c.building AS building,
  COUNT(c.room_number) AS num_classrooms,
  AVG(c.capacity) AS avg_capacity
FROM classroom_rows c
GROUP BY c.building
views.description: Per-building aggregated measures computed from classrooms: count of rooms and average classroom capacity.

views.name: section_room_assignments
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  s.course_id,
  s.sec_id,
  s.semester,
  s.year,
  s.building,
  s.room_number,
  s.time_slot_id
FROM section AS s
views.description: One row per section occurrence with its assigned classroom (building + room_number) and identifying section keys. Useful for questions combining room properties with scheduled sections/instructors/students.

views.name: departments_budget_rank
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  d.dept_name,
  d.building,
  d.budget,
  DENSE_RANK() OVER (ORDER BY d.budget DESC) AS budget_rank
FROM department AS d
views.description: Departments with their budget plus a dense rank over budget (rank 1 = highest budget). Useful for selecting top-budget departments or ties.

views.name: department_buildings
views.body_sql:
SELECT department.dept_name AS dept_name,
       department.building AS building
FROM department
WHERE department.building IS NOT NULL
views.description: List of departments with their associated building(s). One row per department-building association.

views.name: classroom_by_building
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  building,
  COUNT(room_number) AS classroom_count,
  AVG(capacity) AS avg_capacity_raw,
  SUM(capacity) AS capacity_sum
FROM classroom
GROUP BY building
views.description: Classroom rows grouped at the building level with raw measures (counts and average capacity). One row per building.

views.name: department_building_classrooms_join
views.body_sql:
SELECT d.dept_name,
       c.building,
       c.room_number,
       c.capacity
FROM department d
JOIN classroom c
  ON d.building = c.building
views.description: Denormalized join of departments to classrooms for buildings that match the department's building. Each row is one classroom linked to the department that lists that building.

views.name: student_base
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  student.ID AS ID,
  student.name AS name,
  student.dept_name AS dept_name,
  student.tot_cred AS tot_cred
FROM student
views.description: One row per student with core student attributes (identity, name, department, total credits). Useful as the basic student cohort to filter, join, and aggregate for many student-related questions.
validated_on: Hey there! Could you tell me how many unique students have an advisor whose salary is over $30,000 and who taught in the Fall semester, and these students have at least 50 total credits? I'm curious about the count of such students!

views.name: student_with_advisor_instructor
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  s.ID AS ID,
  s.name AS name,
  s.dept_name AS dept_name,
  s.tot_cred AS tot_cred,
  a.i_ID AS i_ID
FROM student AS s
LEFT JOIN advisor AS a
  ON s.ID = a.s_ID
views.description: Denormalized student rows with their advisor instructor ID (if any). One row per student; useful for questions that need student plus advisor linkage or to join to instructor metadata.

views.name: students_taking_section
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  t.ID,
  t.course_id,
  t.sec_id,
  t.semester,
  t.year,
  t.grade
FROM takes AS t
views.description: Row-level relation of students enrolled in specific course sections, exposing student identity plus the section keys (course_id, sec_id, semester, year) and grade. Useful for enrollment/cohort queries, per-section aggregations, and filtering students by courses or terms.

views.name: classroom_capacity_categorized
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  classroom.building AS building,
  classroom.room_number AS room_number,
  classroom.capacity AS capacity,
  CASE
    WHEN classroom.capacity IS NULL THEN NULL
    WHEN classroom.capacity BETWEEN 0 AND 10 THEN 'XS'
    WHEN classroom.capacity BETWEEN 11 AND 30 THEN 'S'
    WHEN classroom.capacity BETWEEN 31 AND 50 THEN 'M'
    WHEN classroom.capacity BETWEEN 51 AND 100 THEN 'L'
    WHEN classroom.capacity > 100 THEN 'XL'
    ELSE 'UNKNOWN'
  END AS capacity_category
FROM classroom
views.description: Canonicalized classroom rows with an added capacity_category column derived from capacity ranges. Does not apply building- or question-specific filters — ready for aggregation or filtering by building or other attributes.

views.name: classroom_counts_by_category
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  c.building,
  CASE
    WHEN c.capacity IS NULL THEN 'unknown'
    WHEN c.capacity < 20 THEN 'small'
    WHEN c.capacity BETWEEN 20 AND 49 THEN 'medium'
    WHEN c.capacity BETWEEN 50 AND 99 THEN 'large'
    ELSE 'very_large'
  END AS capacity_category,
  COUNT(*) AS classroom_count
FROM classroom_rows c
GROUP BY c.building,
  CASE
    WHEN c.capacity IS NULL THEN 'unknown'
    WHEN c.capacity < 20 THEN 'small'
    WHEN c.capacity BETWEEN 20 AND 49 THEN 'medium'
    WHEN c.capacity BETWEEN 50 AND 99 THEN 'large'
    ELSE 'very_large'
  END
views.description: Pre-aggregated counts of classrooms per capacity category and building. Aggregates at the building + capacity_category level so callers can filter by building and further aggregate or sort as needed.

views.name: instructor_core
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  instructor.ID AS ID,
  instructor.name AS name,
  instructor.dept_name AS dept_name,
  instructor.salary AS salary
FROM instructor
views.description: One row per instructor with canonical instructor attributes (ID, name, department, salary). Useful as the base instructor relation for joins and salary-based filters.
validated_on: Hey! Can you tell me how many different instructors were teaching courses in the spring semester of 2023? I'm curious to know the total count!

views.name: advisor_assignment
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  advisor.s_ID AS s_ID,
  advisor.i_ID AS i_ID
FROM advisor
views.description: Advisor assignments linking students to their advisor instructors. One row per student-advisor pair (s_ID, i_ID). Useful to identify which instructors act as advisors.

views.name: advisors_with_salary
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  advisor.s_ID AS s_ID,
  advisor.i_ID AS i_ID,
  instructor.name AS name,
  instructor.salary AS salary,
  instructor.dept_name AS dept_name
FROM advisor
LEFT JOIN instructor ON advisor.i_ID = instructor.ID
views.description: Denormalized view of advisor instructors by joining advisor assignments to instructor attributes. One row per student-advisor assignment annotated with the advisor's salary and name, enabling counts of distinct advisors meeting salary conditions.

views.name: instructors_with_salary_and_teaching_semesters
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  i.ID AS ID,
  i.name AS name,
  i.dept_name AS dept_name,
  i.salary AS salary,
  t.semester AS semester,
  t.year AS year,
  t.course_id AS course_id,
  t.sec_id AS sec_id
FROM instructor i
LEFT JOIN teaches t
  ON i.ID = t.ID
views.description: One row per instructor x semester taught (denormalized): instructor identity and salary plus a semester flag for semesters they taught. Useful to test existence of instructor teaching in a particular semester (e.g., 'Fall').

views.name: advisor_relationships
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  advisor.s_ID AS s_ID,
  advisor.i_ID AS i_ID
FROM advisor
views.description: One row per student-advisor pair linking student ID to instructor ID. Keeps the raw pairing so questions can filter by student attributes or advisor attributes.

views.name: course_by_department
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  course.course_id,
  course.dept_name,
  course.credits,
  course.title
FROM
  course
views.description: One row per course with its department and credits. Useful to identify which departments offer courses meeting credit-based filters.
validated_on: Hey! Can you tell me how many different departments have courses with more than 3 credits?

views.name: departments_with_course_presence
views.body_sql:
SELECT d.dept_name AS dept_name,
       c.course_id AS course_id,
       c.credits AS credits
FROM department d
JOIN course c ON c.dept_name = d.dept_name
views.description: One row per department-course pairing indicating that a department offers a given course. Useful to compute which departments have at least one course satisfying various conditions (e.g., credits threshold).

views.name: courses_core
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  course.course_id AS course_id,
  course.title AS title,
  course.dept_name AS dept_name,
  course.credits AS credits
FROM course
views.description: One row per course with canonical course identifying columns and department/credits exposed. Useful as the base cohort of courses for filters, joins, and aggregates.
validated_on: What are the titles of courses that have exactly two prerequisites?

views.name: course_prereq_pairs
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  c.course_id AS course_id,
  c.title AS title,
  p.prereq_id AS prereq_id
FROM
  course AS c
JOIN
  prereq AS p
ON
  c.course_id = p.course_id
views.description: One row per course-prerequisite relationship, joining course and prereq so course metadata (like title) is available alongside each prereq_id.

views.name: course_prereq_counts
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  c.course_id AS course_id,
  COUNT(DISTINCT p.prereq_id) AS prereq_count
FROM
  course AS c
LEFT JOIN
  prereq AS p
ON
  c.course_id = p.course_id
GROUP BY
  c.course_id
views.description: Count of distinct prerequisite courses per course. One row per course with a raw count measure; does not apply final threshold filters so it can be reused for different counts.

views.name: departments_by_building
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  building,
  COUNT(DISTINCT dept_name) AS distinct_dept_count
FROM department
WHERE building IS NOT NULL AND TRIM(building) <> ''
GROUP BY building
views.description: One row per department building giving the distinct count of departments located in that building and a canonical building value (excludes NULL/empty building values by default in view_filters). Useful for queries that ask how many departments occupy each building or which buildings have a specific number of departments.

views.name: department_locations_detail
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  department.dept_name AS dept_name,
  department.building AS building,
  department.budget AS budget
FROM department

semantic_filters.building: NO DEFAULT (keep all rows; caller may exclude NULL/empty)

views.description: Row-level listing of departments with their building and other department attributes. One row per department (dept_name). Useful for cohort filters, joins to other tables, and for counting/grouping by building at query time.

views.name: buildings_with_department_counts
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  d.building AS building,
  d.dept_name AS dept_name,
  dbb.distinct_dept_count AS distinct_dept_count
FROM department AS d
LEFT JOIN departments_by_building AS dbb
  ON d.building = dbb.building

semantic_filters.building: NO DEFAULT (keep all rows; caller may exclude NULL/empty)

views.description: Per-building denormalized row with building identifier plus aggregated dept count and a sample of department names optionally (keeps department-level granularity via separate rows for each dept_name if caller needs detail). This view exposes building and dept_name and also includes a pre-computed distinct_dept_count (same aggregation as departments_by_building) to speed up common filters while still providing dept-level rows if needed.

views.name: course_prereq_links
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  prereq.course_id AS course_id,
  prereq.prereq_id AS prereq_id
FROM prereq
views.description: Row-level relation of prerequisite links: one row per (course_id, prereq_id) pair. Useful for counting prerequisites per course or exploring prerequisite graphs.

views.name: course_prereq_counts_37
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  c.course_id AS course_id,
  COUNT(DISTINCT p.prereq_id) AS prereq_count
FROM
  course AS c
LEFT JOIN
  prereq AS p
ON
  c.course_id = p.course_id
GROUP BY
  c.course_id
views.description: Aggregate counts of distinct prerequisites per course. One row per course_id with the number of distinct prereq_id values. Does not filter courses with zero prerequisites; those will be absent unless outer-joined from course_core.

views.name: course_prereq_counts_38
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  c.course_id AS course_id,
  COUNT(p.prereq_id) AS prereq_count
FROM
  course c
LEFT JOIN
  prereq p
ON
  c.course_id = p.course_id
GROUP BY
  c.course_id
views.description: Count of prerequisites per course (one row per course.course_id) to identify courses with multiple prereqs.

views.name: departments_with_building
views.body_sql:
SELECT dept_name, building, budget
FROM department
views.description: Department rows with their associated building and budget. Useful for queries that group or filter departments by building or compute statistics (like average budget) per department possibly combined with building-level constraints.

views.name: courses_without_prereqs
views.body_sql:
SELECT c.course_id,
       c.title,
       c.dept_name,
       c.credits
FROM course AS c
LEFT JOIN prereq AS p
  ON c.course_id = p.course_id
WHERE p.prereq_id IS NULL
views.description: All courses that have no prereq entries (courses with zero prerequisites).

views.name: sections_with_classroom
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  s.course_id,
  s.sec_id,
  s.semester,
  s.year,
  c.building,
  c.room_number
FROM section AS s
JOIN classroom AS c
  ON s.building = c.building
  AND s.room_number = c.room_number
views.description: Section occurrences joined to the classroom they use (one row per section instance with its classroom).

views.name: dept_classrooms_for_prereq_free_courses
views.body_sql:
SELECT DISTINCT
  c.dept_name,
  s.building,
  s.room_number,
  cr.capacity
FROM courses_core c
JOIN sections_with_classroom s ON s.course_id = c.course_id
JOIN classroom_core cr ON cr.building = s.building AND cr.room_number = s.room_number
LEFT JOIN course_prereq_pairs p ON p.course_id = c.course_id
WHERE p.prereq_id IS NULL
views.description: Distinct classrooms used by sections of courses (grouped to department) where the course has no prerequisites. One row per distinct (department, classroom) combination as used by at least one section of a prereq-free course.

views.name: courses_count_by_department
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  c.dept_name AS dept_name,
  COUNT(*) AS total_courses_in_department
FROM course AS c
GROUP BY c.dept_name
views.description: Count of courses per department_name (counts every course row grouped by course.dept_name). Keeps dept_name as stored on the course row so NULLs are preserved as distinct keys.

views.name: courses_core_44
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  course.course_id AS course_id,
  course.title AS title,
  course.dept_name AS dept_name,
  course.credits AS credits
FROM course
views.description: Canonical list of courses with their identifying id, title, department, and credits (one row per course). Useful as the core course entity for filtering, joining, and selecting course attributes.

views.name: course_prereq_links_45
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  prereq.course_id AS course_id,
  prereq.prereq_id AS prereq_id
FROM prereq
views.description: Row-level listing of prerequisite relationships: each row represents one prerequisite edge where a course (course_id) requires a prereq (prereq_id). Useful for finding courses that have zero or multiple prereqs, or for graph traversals.

views.name: courses_with_prereq_flag
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  c.course_id,
  c.title,
  c.dept_name,
  c.credits,
  COALESCE(pc.prereq_count, 0) AS prereq_count,
  CASE WHEN COALESCE(pc.prereq_count, 0) > 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS has_prereq
FROM course c
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT course_id, COUNT(prereq_id) AS prereq_count
  FROM prereq
  GROUP BY course_id
) pc ON c.course_id = pc.course_id
views.description: Denormalized course-level view that indicates whether a course has any prerequisite records. One row per course, with a boolean-flag (has_prereq) and raw prereq_count for convenience. Useful for queries needing to filter courses by presence or absence of prerequisites without re-joining prereq every time.

views.name: teaches_row_level
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  t.ID,
  t.course_id,
  t.sec_id,
  t.semester,
  t.year
FROM teaches AS t
views.description: One row per teaching assignment (teaches row). Includes keys to related section and instructor and the semester/year/time identifiers used for filtering.

views.name: section_row_level
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  section.course_id AS course_id,
  section.sec_id AS sec_id,
  section.semester AS semester,
  section.year AS year,
  section.building AS building,
  section.room_number AS room_number,
  section.time_slot_id AS time_slot_id
FROM section
views.description: One row per section (a offered course section in a particular semester/year). Exposes classroom and time_slot keys to allow join/filter by valid sections.
